utterances.text: General, I'd like to go book to this meeting that you had at approximately 11.30 on the 4th of August, 1995, at the RSK headquarters. And if I may, a Mr. Strbac told the Office of the Prosecutor that: "General Forand, and only he, had such vehicles available," talking about the vehicles, the APCs. And then he noted that: "The video team from Yugoslavia happened to be in Knin when the attacks began. They went out to document the shelling. They were assisted by Mr. Forand's men who provided them an armoured vehicle with drivers." Now, Mr. Strbac is an RSK official. General, did you, in fact, provide the RSK with an APC?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a surprise to he me. I never gave permission or direction that way. So this is a complete surprise for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you know if some of the UN personnel were driving around with this --

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would be very surprised because I had given strict orders that we would use those APC only to go and get the people that were supposed to be recalled to my camp. And I know that I had a problem with one of my Jordanian officers who went back to his apartment to get some -- his personal stuff, and I saw that and I was not very pleased. So I made sure that the only reason they were getting -- going out was to go and try to get those people that are -- had not made it back into the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: "Those" being the UN employees?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So any other use was unauthorised?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only other use is that if they were finding some wounded people, they were bringing them to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, with regard to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm just slowing down for the sake of the translators.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So when Colonel Kosta Novakovic told the OTP that he proceeded to the Knin hospital - and this is the morning of the 4th - proceeded to the Knin hospital in a UN APC, you don't know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sir, as for the actual dealing with RSK soldiers, when refugees or people came to your gate on the evening of the 4th, the UN Sector South did allow ARSK soldiers into the compound, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I'm aware of. What we did is that when I decided to let them in, those that were at the gate, we did conduct a search, and there was some weapons, you know, that were found. But I don't know who was an ARSK soldier or not. To me, you know, they were displaced people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What weapons did you find?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I would have to be reminded, you know, of what we collected.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, you remember Major Bellerose, do you not, Claude Bellerose?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, he was my engineer officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may bring up a interview he gave via Sanction. That's it. And if we can go to the next page and on the right-hand side where it says: "Yes. There were some civilians and some military." Can we raise that a bit?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It says: "Yes. There were some military," he says," because we opened up the camp to displaced people to provide security. There were few Serb soldiers that came to try to get refuge within our camp. So we said to them, 'If you want to come in you, have to disarm because if we let you in with weapons, we were's putting ourselves at risk.'" Now, that is one of our officers talking about allowing ARSK soldiers into the compound. Were you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware that some were found with weapons, you know, when we searched them; but I don't recall, you know, if it was specifically mentioned there were ARSK soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, you talked to us about, on the 5th, evacuating individuals from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me show you a clip from the UN Sector South, 1D28-0035.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, as far as the previous document is concerned, we want --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm not going to offer it at this time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a -- I don't believe -- is the sound okay on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that some improvement has been made as far as sound is concerned, and that a provisional solution is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, with regard to this tape, I don't believe there is any sound on it, or that we're not going to require the sound. If I may play this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, that particular video was taken at your compound, and was that an RSK soldier that you evacuated from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not there, you know, for every people that was coming into that camp. I gave the direction, "Let them in, search them, and then segregate them." And when I told Colonel Leslie, "We'll also evacuate the wounded from the hospital," I was not there, you know, to verify each one that was coming in. I was not there at all. I was in my OPs room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. Just a for foundational purposes, if it's either the case -- excuse me, that the witness recognises the location of the video, or if we can have a representation about the -- how it is that we know where the video was taken from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, this was produced by the Prosecution as part of a longer segment of any number of items that had been filmed, and produced to us in UN Sector South headquarters. We just extracted this one piece.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But, nevertheless, that doesn't invalidate what Mr. Tieger thinks, at least I understand his words, what the Chamber needs. I mean, you bring us someone in a bed, and you say, Is this an ARSK soldier brought into the hospital. The witness says: "I don't know." Either we leave it to that; or if you want to give it any follow-up, then, of course, we have to establish what the location is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Absolutely, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From the quick view, I didn't see him being in uniform or armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: He was not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you need a bit more to give it a useful follow-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, did you recognise that area as the hospital area in UN Sector South?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that was the gym which we transformed, I wouldn't call it a hospital, but a place where we could put the sick and the wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Approximately when were you bringing the sick and the wounded into the gym that you had reconfigured as a hospital?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was the 5th, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, going back to that, sir, you took sick and wounded from this particular location, from the hospital, and if I may show you D277.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, the video played, do we have to need that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I just offer that into evidence at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we could please have a number, yes, we are offering that into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It was a bit unclear to me whether --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, any objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D330, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D330 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, you were aware that in August and July of 1995, the RSK was under full mobilisation for all males to go into the ARSK; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Is it your belief, as looking at this taking a video, whether or not that video was or was not a soldier?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: If he was a soldier?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was he a soldier?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if he was a soldier. He was of age, for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we look at D277, if we go to the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Starting with the paragraph -- in the second paragraph: "The Knin hospital remains structurally sound with no evidence of artillery or mortar damage ..." That's consistent with what you said this morning; correct, General?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said this morning is that I was told that there was potentially a round that had hit the hospital, but there was no -- it was not a target, per se.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, when you got there, you didn't see any damage to the hospital, did you?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because I didn't go around the hospital. I went directly in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we go a couple of sentences down: "When the Croatian medical personnel arrived on 6 August, they found 20 elderly patients in the basement of the hospital." Is that accurate, General, you left the elderly patients in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I left those that, when I spoke to the doctor that they were - don't know what's the word - hat they needed treatment constantly on life - whatever it's called - because I when I spoke to him, the chance of them making it alive to my camp, because of the transport, was not very high. So I decided that they would not bring them to my camp because, first, they could die en route, or I did not have the capability, you know, for self-sustainment in my camp. So I left those people - I don't know how many there were - but I left them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So, General, then why did you move the wounded?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we were able to take care of them. And at that time, remember, in my presentation, I was told that, you know, the hospital had been hit, and I was afraid that they could be others. So I decided that based on that information, which I did not verify, to move the wounded and the sick to my headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So the people that were very sick, you didn't move; but people that could move, you did move?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, again, if I could find the right word. [Interpretation] Those who could not be displaced, those who could not be moved.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The witness also said: "Those in palliative care could not be moved."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And did the group that you moved, General, include men of military age?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Like I said, we moved all of those --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we have a bit of a problem because if you change the French, which is then translated, but I think we missed when you were talking about "soins palliatifs". That's a portion which is, if I read well, is missing after "those who could not be moved." I now change to French for a second. [Interpretation] There is no problem if you want to speak French; however, you should tell us about it first, so that we are informed about it. [In English] And if you want to hear the French, for example, if I speak French, then if you move from channel 4 to channel 5, you will receive the French original or French translation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, my answer on -- question on line 9 was: Did the group that you moved include men of military age?"

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as you saw on the video, there was some, but I was not there at the reception. And when I went myself to the hospital, because the only people that were left to be moved were those people that I felt, you know, might die on me, so I didn't bring any back with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, was it a violation of the UN mandate to move soldiers from any of the warring factions?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: If they were recognised as soldiers, yeah, I suppose; but if they are wounded or sick, to me, you know, it's humanitarian help that we were providing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So, according to your rationale, moving wounded soldiers is within your mandate?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say it was within my mandate. I said it was humanitarian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, instead of putting your next question, it's also good to listen to the answers, because whether they were soldiers or not is your conclusion and not what the witness said. He said they were of military age and, therefore, they could have been soldiers. Let's try to keep things straight.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, let me talk to you a little bit about the morning of the 4th, and you noted for us in your transcript that you - and this is on page 4115, on line 1 and 2 - that you "... stayed about ten minutes at the most, you know, looking at the artillery barrage that was taking place." Now, let me turn your attention to D270. Looking at D270, General, it's a letter from General Mrksic at 0330 hours -- 0630 hours on the 4th, to General Janvier in Zagreb. Essentially, it's protesting the shelling. In the third paragraph down, it notes: "We demand that you take immediate measures to stop the aggression." Were you made aware of this, General?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You shown it to me, I think, yesterday or the day before. That was the first time I had seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us turn attention to 1D28-0021. Your Honour, there is a French version of this as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, in this, this is a message from General Mrksic to General Janvier, if you can just take a quick look at it, talking about the shelling. On the sixth line down, it says that: "They," talking about the HV, "also targeted the hospital and other similar buildings, firing randomly and without any order. UNPROFOR officers located there can confirm these claims." Now, General, when you went in the morning of the 4th to ARSK or RSK headquarters, did you know about these protests.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you did know, sir, that approximately 6.30 in the morning that there had been some incoming mortar fire into the camp?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my camp?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Into your camp.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: We never -- there was no bomb of whatever kind that fell in my camp, you know, throughout the whole period.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm reminded, sir, on the radio broadcast, that they were talking about on the 4th, you mentioned that there was some incoming fire on the camp on the 4th.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think I said near the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, that particular fire near the camp, that was relatively close to your camp on the morning of the 4th?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think -- did I specify the morning of the 4th?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm asking you, sir.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was only one shell that landed five to ten metres from the north-west corner of my camp, and there was six or seven civilians that were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's on the 5th, sir.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's on the 5th. On the 4th, there was no -- I think I make it very clear in my presentation that the closest it had come was 350 to 400 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I just note for the record, General, that the radio interview of this morning where you mention this was the morning of the 4th. But you have no recollection of that?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, and I don't recall that it was on that tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, you went to this meeting on the -- at the ARSK headquarters, you said, at 11.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can turn to Exhibit 341 -- that's P341, excuse me. Before we move on, Your Honour, we'll offer up 1D28-0021 into evidence, which is the --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I anticipated that it would be coming. Briefly, all I have on this at the moment is a typed-out English document without any headings or indication of provenance, so I need information before I can respond to the tender.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, it's uploaded in e-court, and I see an - let me just look -- I see an original in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I will clarify this with the Prosecution. It was the part of a bundle of documents that was provided, that came from Mr. Akashi that had been sent to the UN. And it was in that bundle that was provided, and I can clarify the source with counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, if it was in the bundle, was that bundle already admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I must say that the original was in French, and we will see -- and the numbers is R09095.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's see. We're still talking about the letter sent to General Bertrand Janvier. Is that complained by Republika Srpska, or are am I behind?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. This is the message from General Mrksic to General Janvier that was transmitted by Colonel Kosta Novakovic by telephone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you say the original was --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I understand it correctly, there are two separate documents. One, I think, is represented by what I -- I don't have the uploaded version in front of me, but I think that is the message from the protest letter from Mrksic to Janvier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 4th of August, 0630 hours, protest against the shelling of civilian targets.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Right. I think that's a previous exhibit. This is indicated, according to the English, as a message transmitted by Colonel Novakovic by telephone. And as Mr. Kehoe indicated, I think the original of the English is translated from French and is something different; although, I haven't seen the French.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, the French appears on, I'm informed by my colleagues, at 65 ter 411.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if you would like to move on. I doubt there is an objection, but, as I say, I wasn't in a position to respond in the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's give it a number, and I take it that you sought out what is original and what exactly the document is. Mr. Registrar, the document, on our screen, the message from General Mrksic to General Janvier, will have number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D331, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, if you would have sorted out what it actually is, would the content raise any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. It's a matter of the provenance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then D331 is admitted into evidence, and the Prosecution has not more than one week to revisit the provenance. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, if we move to Exhibit 341, this is a sitrep, and I note it's at August 4th, at 1400 hours. This is after your meeting at the RSK headquarters, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, prior to your meeting, prior to this sitrep, had you had written reports and documentation coming from any of your battalions in the field that there was indiscriminate shelling of civilian areas taking place in the Krajina?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, yes, because that's what I based -- from what I had seen in Knin and the reports coming from my unit, that's what I based the sense of the letter that I sent to General Gotovina on the 4th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So, in your recollection, there was written documentation coming from your battalions on shelling of civilian areas; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if it was written. It was passed, you know, to my OPs officer, who then passed it on to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, you would agree with me, in going to page 2 of this document and the top of this page, in the third paragraph -- second paragraph down, this report of "shelling of Knin and other towns is reported to be indiscriminate and is continuing sporadically," that is the first written document in UN Sector South calling this shelling indiscriminate, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, when you were preparing for your testimony, were you shown any other document prior to this that -- prior to this sitrep, that described the shelling as indiscriminate? Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, based on --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us turn to P83.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, this is your protest letter. Now, did you write this or was this sent out in the afternoon of the 4th of August?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did I what?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was this letter -- was this letter sent out in the afternoon of the 4th of August?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, again, this was sent out after your meeting at the RSK?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was in the afternoon, for sure, because the meeting was according to the sitrep at around 11.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's look at these cities in here. The cities that you mention --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can just blow up that first paragraph just a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's just pick a few out: Medak. You note that there was artillery fire on the towns of Drnis, Medak and others, numerous civilian casualties caused. Now, with regard to Medak itself, were there military positions of the RSK in Medak that were fired upon?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, let me take a look at your presentation at page 29.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's P401.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Actually, that's good because this starts at we're talking about the 5th of August, and you can see --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can go to the next page, the third to last paragraph: "Meanwhile ..." -- excuse me, fourth to last paragraph. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: "Meanwhile in the Medak valley," this is on the 5th, "the HV broke the Serb defence at Medak by mid-afternoon on the 5th." So, General, throughout the 4th and into mid-afternoon on the 5th, there was significant fighting in the Medak area, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That seems to be the case, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What civilian facilities in Medak were hit with artillery fire?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you that. Like I said, I got the report from my unit; and you will see in one of the sitrep, that we're saying that we would like to have verification, because when we received the report, usually we ask them, you know, to go and verify if it is exact, you know, what they are putting in the sitrep. But you must appreciate that during that period, there was report coming from all over my unit; and, unfortunately, we did not have the capacity to go and verify. So everything was based, and it was clearly stated in one of my initial sitrep, that we could not verify the exactitude of that. But what I had seen when I was on the balcony, to me, again, I repeat, it seems to be indiscriminate because it was falling -- the smoke was coming from all the area in Knin; and the report that I was receiving from my unit, in those towns that were specifically mentioned, was the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can go back to P83, and if we can blow that up just a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, this particular letter lists the cities and the reports the allegations that you put in here after the war was ended. Let's just start with Medak. Did you go back and check?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you order anybody to go back and check?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's turn to -- well, before we do that, General, this letter was being sent to Zagreb for dissemination throughout the international community, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was sent to our military observer officer to pass on to the LO, that it then would be passed to General Gotovina. It was sent to the world at large.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But it's CC'd at the bottom, and the copy is to?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Commander UNCRO, my boss.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Al Rodin?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And did you have the expectation that it was going to be disseminated to the world as a part of a media campaign?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no expectation. I was reporting to my boss. What he did with it afterwards, you know, that was out of my hands. But in response to what you were talking about, that we didn't go and see in Medak, nobody asked me from Croat side, which they were aware of that letter, to go and visit and make an inquiry after the trouble were finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you ask, General?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did they ask me? No, they didn't ask me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, General. You made the allegation in this letter. Did you ask to go visit?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not, and they did not ask me either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, to the extent that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- your point is that you want to raise doubt as to the accuracy of the factual description of what appears in this letter, which is written in rather a chaotic situation, then that point has been made. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, just turning to Bunic very quickly. It also lists Bunic, and if we can take a look at the sitrep Exhibit 340; P340, I might add.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is a sitrep of 4 August at 1020, and going to the section. The next page, talking about Bunic in the middle of the page: Bunic is in a critical situation. ARSK suffered large casualties in Bunic. General Sevo -- Colonel Sevo, excuse me. You know Colonel Sevo, don't you, General?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met him once.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: "Colonel Sevo ordered to take transport means from there. CESBAT soldiers did not want give that to them." Now, just staying with Bunic, you were aware that this was the forward command post of the Lika Corps, also a command post for the 18th Infantry Battalion of the ARSK, were you not?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now staying with P83, sir, you noted for us that it was -- let me change that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can go back to P83, and if we go to the bottom of that page, all the way to the bottom on the fax line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It reflects a transmission, if you can see at the bottom, of the 12th of August. General, do you have any transmission or any document that this was actually transmitted to General Gotovina or his liaison officer?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I mentioned before when I signed that letter and I passed it on to my OPs officer, it was either Colonel Tymchuk or Major balance four, I specifically stated I want to be sure that this letter reached the individual and he came back a little later on that it was passed on to the military observer that was in Zadar that he had passed it on to Captain Lukovic who would pass it on to General Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you don't know if either Tymchuk or Balfour told you that?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If they come here, you should ask them that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you get any written confirmation that it had been sent?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you know who the person was in Zadar that is UNMO in Zadar that got this?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was supposed to have gotten it?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked me the same question the other day, and I said no, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, with regard to this, let me show you a video that you haven't seen before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's 1D28-0028, and I do believe that this is fine at this point, Your Honour. I did have some transmission problems before. It's an HTV report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any text?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, a text has been given to the booth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can we start from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters need a little bit of time to find the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, if we can just start it from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the interpreters tell us when they are ready?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "General Forand, Commander of Sector South, sent a letter to General Gotovina in which civilians were being killed and CESBAT by observation posts hit in Gospic and Otocac area ..." --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, first of all, of course, I noticed the difference. I did not know what you provided to the booth. There could be a mistake. We're all human beings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's start this video again on from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the booth has the transcript in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine. Let's start again.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] The Brigadier-General Forand, Sector South commander, sent a letter to the commander of the Gospic military district, Brigadier Mirko Norac, vehemently protesting against the artillery attacks on Knin, Drnis, and Bukovac, in which civilians were being killed, and CESBAT observation posts hit in the Gospic and Otocac area. He requested that the Croatian army should withdraw from the separation zone, as well as there was no reason for the attack and no provocation by the Serbs. The barracks in Knin and Petrinja, the command posts of the corps and brigades, and the radio relay transmitter at Celavac, locations that were targeted by the Croatian army artillery, could by no means have been civilian buildings with unarmed Serb civilians inside."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, I'd like to show you one other document - this would be P84 - before I ask you some questions about this video in conjunction with that document. P84 is a document from Colonel Leslie. This is on the 12th of August and written by Colonel Leslie, and he refers on the paragraph 5 to your protest letter, that's two pages in. Do you see that one sentence: "Attached is a formal letter of protest sent by Brigadier-General Forand to Ante Gotovina referred to paragraph 4, referring to this letter that we've been discussing on the 4th. Now, if we may, you note that this memo is on the 12th. Let's just go back to P83. Now we note at the bottom on the fax line at the bottom of the page, as we mentioned before, General, that this was faxed by your office on the 12th of -- excuse me, on the 12th of August, and we also note that it is mentioned in Colonel Leslie's memo. Did Colonel Leslie, to your knowledge, call back down to Sector South headquarters to get a copy of this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm not a fax expert, Your Honour, but I don't know whether that is a fax from or to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'll ask the General a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, one second, one second. You say, Mr. Kehoe: "And we also note that it is mentioned in Colonel Leslie's memo."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: "It" being this letter, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The letter is mentioned in Colonel Leslie's memo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's back at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because you are, by putting these composite questions, you are very much drawing the attention to the fax line and that it was faxed on the 12th. Then you say: "And we also note that it is mentioned," and then you are not talking about fax lines anymore, you're talking about the letter as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We should try to avoid that the gist of the question is missed by a witness. Please put your question again unless you - let me just see - it is mentioned in Colonel Leslie's memo, this letter. Please put your question, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, based on your working in Sector South, the fax line at the bottom means that it was sent from Sector South; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I mean, it doesn't make sense. It was written on the 4th, and I specifically asked that it be sent to our military observer that it would be faxed on the 12th. It doesn't make sense to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, was Colonel Leslie calling back down to you asking for a copy of this letter?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: He already had a copy because I had sent one on the 4th to the UNCRO commander, and he was now on the -- at that date, the Chief of Staff of UNCRO headquarter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So do you not have knowledge about him calling down to get this letter?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, during the course of this particular --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We'll offer the video into evidence, 1D28-0028.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D332, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. D332 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, you noted in your -- yesterday when we were talking about the defences by the ARSK forces, that you were thinking that if they had additional time, they could buy time and get some possible intervention from the UN. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall saying UN intervention. What I'm saying is that if they would have had secondary and tertiary defensive position, they could have maybe stopped, you know, the Croat from advancing, and then maybe the UN could have intervened to try to reestablish peace.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, as part of getting that particular intervention from the UN, it was important for you and the people in UN Sector South to give information out to the world as to what was happening, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not important. Our job was to report, and we were reporting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, General, when you wrote this letter, were you exaggerating the facts so that it would come to the attention, not only of the UN in Zagreb, but also the diplomatic community?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. We reported -- what is in that letter is what I had seen and what I was getting from my unit. It was not an exaggeration. To me, it represented the situation that I was portrayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, did you ever, during the course of your time there, did you or any of your officers exaggerate a particular situation for political or diplomatic effect?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me turn your attention to 1D28-0022. Now, earlier I think you mentioned that the two people that you would have sent this or given this letter to for transmission were either Colonel Tymchuk or Major Balfour. I'm talking about the 4th August letter, and I note that the drafter of this sitrep of 9 August 1995 is Major Balfour. And if we can go to the second paragraph, it goes to the National Defence Headquarters in Canada from HQ Sector South. The subject is "Sector South update sitreps." And it notes in this paragraph on 1800 hours: "I suspect that UNPF sitreps may exaggerate the situation for political diplomatic effect. No real problem here with drinking water or food, even feeding 700 refugees." Now, General, that is an officer that is under your direct command who told the -- your authorities, the National Defence authorities, that UNPF sitreps were exaggerating the water and food issue -- questions that were taking place within UN Sector South.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, would you please quote as what it says, that he "suspects."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: "I suspect."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not the same as --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That he suspects that the UNPF sitreps may exaggerate the situation for political and diplomatic effect. Now, what can you tell us about that exaggeration that Major Balfour suspects that was being for diplomatic -- political or diplomatic effects?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, sir. You would have to ask him. I don't know what he -- I never saw that sitrep. Obviously, that was going from him to a certain person at National Defence Headquarters in Ottawa, but I've never seen that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well General, Major Balfour was the drafter of many of the sitreps that you released that were being sent up to Zagreb headquarters, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those that I've signed, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But you don't know anything about this particular --

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this one, I don't see my name on that, you know, and I don't remember ever being briefed about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, we'll offer 1D28-0022 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D333, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D333 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, staying on that issue of publicity and buying time, you noticed, yesterday when we talking about buying time, consistent with what you said today on page 4356, that: "In your mind, you know, if there was sufficient capability for the ARSK to defend, potentially the UN may have put some pressure on both sides to resume the peace. That's what I had in mind." Now, there was a program -- I'm just letting them catch up, General. Now, there was a programme in effect called "Active Presence" at this time, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: What's that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me show you D288.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is a item called "Active Presence," dated 24 July at 1400 hours, and I submit to you that it was signed by Major-General Al Rodin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we turn to the second page, and if we can just go to the mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, the mission of UNCRO after this order was "to support the political process through the prevention of renewed hostilities," wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that. I would have to read the whole document, and then it would come back.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, maybe, then we can come back to it?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. If you give me a copy of that, I can read it during dinner, but it doesn't ring a bell presently.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, was there a mission afoot to -- let's go back to your actual actions. When you got there in July, you began to put more personnel in your observation posts, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. My plan was to increase the numbers of observation posts in certain area; but we started, I think, on the 1st of August to move certain element from the, if I remember well, from the Czech, the Jordanian, and the Canadian. It was envisaged also to create more observation posts in the Dinara where the Kenyans were located.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you did that almost as soon as you started to come, did you not?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean as soon as I arrived in theatre?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, after you had examined the situation.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I started to plan around those ways.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, and, Mr. Forand, if you could observe small breaks, it certainly would assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we could just go -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But you did, in fact, give them an order, sir, that they were not to withdraw from their positions in the case of conflict without your order; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Why don't you turn to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 6 of this document. One page after that, if we can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It notes in paragraph A, under 4, Action under renewed hostilities: "A, UNCRO forces shall remain in location upon renewed hostilities. All actions necessary for self-defence shall be taken. UNCRO forces shall not withdraw, nor shall positions be abandoned, without authorisation. Warring parties are to be informed of our intentions ..." Now, General, that is consistent with what you were doing, is it not?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, did you do that -- I'm sorry. Did you do that in consultation with General Rodin?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I had started before I received this to increase the security of my observation posts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, likewise, after that, were you in communication with General Rodin that this is, in fact, what you were doing?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was aware that we were improving our security, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, in addition to doing that, General, you had a public information officer by the name of Mr. Roberts?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was not under my command. He was part of UNCRO at the headquarter, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did your personnel give him information to disseminate?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was receiving briefing like other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you also had, and we saw during the course of this trial, General Leslie was commenting for the media about, for instance, what was happening both prior to and during Operation Storm. Was he doing that with your authorisation?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware that he did it before the 4th; that's possible. During the 4th and the 5th, I did only two interviews, and it was either Mr. Roberts or Colonel Leslie, you know, that was conducting the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we can turn to this page prior to this page. If we note, this is a phased programme for Sector South. And at the break, we'll give you an opportunity to read this yet further. It notes: "Phase 1(i), Develop and implement a public information campaign," and then it talks about making decisions on disposition of forces. "Phase 2, Continue the active public campaign," and you redeploy those forces. Now, you did have a information campaign or did have a programme for public information that you wanted to disseminate out of UN Sector South using Mr. Roberts and Colonel Leslie, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that. I would have to read the whole document exactly, you know - they are making a reference to an annex - to see exactly what were they looking for, you know, as far as a public information plan or campaign.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let's look at phase 3, if we can, and (ii), and (ii) notes: "When and where possible, interpose between the warring parties on the Dinara mountains ..." Now, that's what you were telling your troops to do, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I was planning to do, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, this -- you were doing that, as we discussed before, in an effort - I'm talking about interposing your troops between the warring factions - to buy time for the UN to intervene, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not to buy time. The only reason is that I wanted to have a better idea within the zone of separation than I was getting, because the distance between some observation posts was up to three to four kilometre. And because of the activity that was taking place, I said I wanted to have more and better information. It was not to give more time, it was to have better information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I don't know if it's helpful or not, Your Honour. The document that's being discussed is from August 1st, predating --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, it's not. It's the 24th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Okay. Correct. In any event, predating Storm was the point. The discussion about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's not start commenting on the material.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Essentially, the witness is being confronted with previous testimony that is related to a different time period and a different subject, frankly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, the witness is answering questions at this moment which Mr. Kehoe puts to him in relation to a document from General Janvier to Kofi Annan, which as far as I've been able to locate at this moment sets out a lot of things not necessarily saying who is tasked with exactly what to do but that's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Forand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. The document I have on my screen is not Mr. Kofi Annan, it seems to be a directive from General Rodin to his sector commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, you see what happens if we are dealing with documents in this way because this is, as a matter of fact, it is a document sent by Mr. Janvier to Mr. Annan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's at least what I read on the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It is, Judge, and what it is, it includes a copy of -- it notes is it's a copy of headquarter UNCRO's OP order dated 24 July 1995 is attached for your information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Let's move on, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, just -- and you will get an opportunity to look at this. If we can look at page 2 at the top of the page. It notes that as -- "Under friendly forces of the role of the UNPF in Zagreb will support active presence with high level diplomatic and press campaign designed to show that UNCRO is doing all that can be done to implement SCR 981 and that is UNCRO's withdrawal will lead to an intensification of the conflict." Now, General let's just take this sequentially. Prior to Operation Storm, you put additional observation posts out in the Zone of Separation?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was planning to and I think I was able to implement maybe two observation posts in the Czech and the Canadian Battalion area, that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you told the commanders, both on the ARSK side and General Gotovina that you were going to do it whether they liked it or not?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there to inform them that that was my intention and to see from them, you know, if it created any major problem then obviously I would have had to adjust, but basically I was not asking their permission. And I also tried to meet with General Norac which I did, one time, I don't remember if it was for that instance or before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And turning to Operation Storm, UN Sector South had a series of transmissions that you began mid-day being sent up to Zagreb where you described the shelling by the HV forces as indiscriminate; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In addition to that, you had Mr. -- you didn't have, you didn't have Mr. Roberts, but Mr. Roberts and Colonel Leslie were on the media sources describing what was taking place; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that I had to ask Colonel Leslie to respond to a major query because I did not have the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, this is the same Colonel Leslie that this morning described the shelling during Operation Storm killing between 10.000 and 25.000, it's the same?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was only one Colonel Leslie in my headquarter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was the operation in UN Sector South, Colonel -- excuse me, General, engaged in a series of exaggerations during Operation Storm so that you could buy time for UN intervention?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's three time you ask me the same question and I say no again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, General --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness is correctly drawing your attention to the fact that these questions become repetitious.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On the subject, one more question, Mr. Kehoe, but let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour I'm moving on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apparently you've --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we turn to the situation of the UN personnel that were taken by the HV in - I'm trying to get the exhibit - P343, if we can bring that up on the screen. If we can go to page 5 of that document. Is that page 5. I'm talking about page 5 on the top, if we can go page -- three more pages in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, there is a protocol that you should refer to the page of the document as it appears in e-court because where you earlier referred to page 2, that page was on the top page 3 and was page 3 in the -- so whenever we turn to pages, it should be the pages as they appear in the e-court uploaded document. Please proceed. Do we have the right page now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, at the bottom of that page, it is being described as acts against UNPROFOR. "Deliberate attacks, HV troops surrounded and disarmed a lot of OPs in sector. Some UN soldiers from these OPs were taken to the Croatian side of the Zone of Separation. HV troops have taken a total of 40 KenBat soldiers as hostages ..." Now, in other correspondence, did you also describe them as prisoners?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: You will have to show me the other correspondence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, before we move to the other correspondence, with regard to these particular Kenyan soldiers, at the time did you ask for close air support or for the Canadians, were you asking for close air support to deter the HV from moving into those areas?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was one instance where we requested that UNCRO headquarter and air support for the Canadian, and another instance where it was requested for the Czech who they were having a problem with some Muslim organisation from the Bihac area, I remember there were five BiH, or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you were -- in this close air support, this was going up to Zagreb, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes, because I did not have the authority over those people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And in that particular instance, when you were asking for this close air support, it was the threat to bomb these people, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was used as a threat to the Croats so that -- okay -- it was used as a threat to the Croat so that they would not expel the Canadian from the observation posts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: My question was it was a threat to bomb these people, that these troops, wasn't it? That's a different ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. We have to wait for the French translation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't have on my screen the question as they are typed. Is it possible to have it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that there's no problem if you would read the transcript, and then you are also invited as long as the text is still moving, we are still working on it, so if you could wait for the answer until it has stopped moving.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because Your Honour, I did not have on my screen the writing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Mr. Kehoe, perhaps now you repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, I understand that the attempt was to deter the HV from moving into the area, but that also comes with the threat to bomb these units, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was the aim, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Otherwise there is no threat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And was that likewise -- obviously you told us that went up to Zagreb. Was that likewise something you contemplated when the Kenyans were taken, as you described, as hostages?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because the -- we had good communication with the Canadian but the communication with the Kenyan, when I learned about it, they were already, you know, in the hand of the Croat, so it was too late.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you ordered this close air support, for instance, in the CanBat area when you knew that there was a co-location problem with ARSK forces next to OPs isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, may I take it that you wanted to say, Now you requested this close --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Requested, exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that was the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Isn't that right, sir, you requested close air support when you knew that there was a co-location problem with ARSK forces next to the OPs?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, there was no ARSK force close to the OP.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: To your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You were not being shown the situation reports that were coming in that ARSK forces were near your OPs?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the Canadian area, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, suffice it to say, sir, that that -- let's turn our attention to 1D28-0017. The bottom of the page on paragraph 3, this is going to -- from Janvier, General Janvier to Kofi Annan on the 5th of August, under 3. "I regret the confusion caused by the use of the term "prisoners" in reference C, however, the initial HV advance and the systematic clearing of UN OPs created considerable confusion. Thus it was assumed that the UN soldiers who had been taken by the HV were in fact prisoners. Recent returns of some of these personnel would indicate that the HV are in fact forcibly escorting UN soldiers to other locations but are not treating them as prisoners." Now, General, in your initial correspondence with Zagreb, were you describing these people as prisoners?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as you saw, it was hostage but I think I came to the same conclusion that -- as Mr. Akashi that wrote this letter, because we found out afterwards that our soldier had been well treated by the Croats but at the time, I did not have that particular information and at that time, the information that I had was they were forcibly removed. Well, in my view when you forcibly remove, they were being taken hostages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Forand, I have one very general question for you which is the following: In your reporting, did you ever, on purpose, exaggerate either for media purposes or for political purposes or have you always reported to the best of your knowledge about what you thought at that moment was reality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. In my view, I have never exaggerated. It was based on the information I was receiving and that's what I was passing along. Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, this is a rather general question and we heard a lot of questions and a lot of answers which all apparently were in the same context, and I think that you could move on. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, just turning your attention to 1D28-0001, paragraph 5. This is a United States Department of Defence cable of 6 August, paragraph 5. Now, likewise that says on -- the first sentence, "Claims reports of deliberate targeting of UN OPs and other positions are not accurate." That's true, sir, isn't it? That the observation posts were not deliberately targeted, were they?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were some that were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, you talked about -- and let me go to D229 -- D29. You talked about the shelling of Knin in the course of your testimony and your statements, and looking at paragraph 2, this is by Mr. Akashi to Mr. Annan. "My overall impression of the town of Knin is that it suffered considerable damage from artillery fire, which was evident in the streets, where I observed many shops with broken windows, cars damaged and off the road, artillery shell holes in the road, et cetera. However, the damage to the town's structures, while noticeable, was less than I anticipated." Now, were you informed of that, General, that the damage that was -- people expected to see such as Mr. Akashi on the 7th, was less than anticipated?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Akashi did not confide in me, you know, that he had seen that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, as you sit here today, was the information that was provided to you by your subordinates such as Colonel Leslie concerning things like the shelling of Knin greatly exaggerated as was his estimates of the amount killed during that shelling?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't consider it exaggerated. I had total confidence, you know, in his capability to assess and he was an artillery officer, so he was in a better position, you know, to comment on that shelling than almost anybody else in the headquarter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So you relied on what General Leslie was saying and doing when you were making your decisions?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was my Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, let me turn our attention to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, when you were talking about his estimates, what estimates were you referring to? The ones in the broadcast or in the reporting or ... because I think that 10.000 to 25.000 had been dealt with. I think that the witness has answered that. So it's not clear to me what estimates you are now talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I will go back to a particular item. And I was trying to -- I possibly moved through this too quickly. Q. I want to go back to your testimony, General, that you said on page 4115 that you were on -- looking at the shelling for about ten minutes. Then on line 8, and you are discussing other personnel up there, "It seemed to those that were observing that shelling that was also indiscriminate and in their view, there was no military target there." You said that, I believe, the day before yesterday. The person that you were talking about was Colonel Leslie, wasn't it.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember Colonel Leslie being there when I was there. There was five or six other officers from my headquarter, but I don't remember Colonel Leslie being there at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was Colonel Leslie talking to you during the course of the day that he had concluded that this fire was indiscriminate and that it was not -- it was not directed towards military targets?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we must have spoken during the day for sure, before I wrote the letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you would naturally in the course of things rely on the information that Colonel Leslie gave you while you would be writing this letter?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: For sure. On him and others also.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, General, let me show you, if I may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, I am looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may finish this one subject, I will be a couple of minutes, Judge, and I will be out of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, this is the recommendation -- if you go to the next page. And then the next page. This is the recommendation signed by you for Colonel Leslie proposing him for an award, and if we can go to the next page?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I read that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if we can go to the next page, it's the recommendation for a meritorious service cross. And if we can go down to report 2. "During the initial intense artillery barrage on Knin on 4 August 1995, Colonel Leslie realised that approximately 40 UN employees were trapped in their residences in the downtown area. Without concern for his own safety, he organised and participated in several rescue missions to collect them and bring them to the relative safety of the UN camp using armoured personnel carriers. His decisive intervention almost certainly saved many UN employees from serious injury or death." Now --

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you higher and see where -- is it attached to the -- what you showed me before?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What's that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: What's on top of that page?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is a sequence of pages --

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know but it is related to the other document or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it's one central -- one document of multiple pages. I can go back and just show you the other pages?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I just thought there was something written at the top. I'm looking at the date, November.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's when it was provided to -- it looks like the Department of Justice. It's a recent item. This is back -- the date of this submission by you, General, is -- you signed it on 10 October 1995.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: But this seems to indicate November. I'm trying to remember if I signed only the first part. This, I don't remember and you know how the system works for a medal in Canada?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, General, specifically, I do not. Other than this was provided by the National Defence as the package for this submission for General Leslie.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the way it works, Your Honour, is that I make a recommendation but because I was a sector commander, I was not considered by the Canadian as a Canadian but as a UN member. I had to send that recommendation to the contingent commander, who was a Mr. Daigle, Colonel Daigle on the first page, then he has to send it to the National Defence Headquarters where it is a committee that sits, and then if it is agreed, they recommend the individual for a medal. The individual is not aware that he will receive a medal until it is announced that he will receive a medal, and he does not know the content of the citation until he goes in front of the Governor General and then it's read to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, this recommendation if you go to page 2 was signed by you.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. Then --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just turn the page -- the next page of this document. That's your signature at the bottom of this page, is it not?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It sure is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And let us turn back to the prior page and the report two. Going back to that General, when it talks about General Leslie's activities, " ... saving 40 UN employees --" saying, "His decisive intervention almost certainly saved many UN employees from serious injury or death." That, General, is an exaggeration of what he did, isn't it, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: In what sense, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, he didn't do it, did he?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't do it personally, but he organised without concern, he organised and participated. He -- I remember that he went at least on two of those recuperation, but the aim here is that he organised, you know, those trips to go and get those people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It notes here, sir, that he participated in several rescue missions and he didn't, did he?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, I thought he had participated in at least two.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Are you aware, General, that on page -- that General Leslie told this Court at page 2117 that he said, "The first time I became aware of this citation and I was unaware that it was being prepared, was when it was at the Government House, the conclusion of this I spoke to the vice chief defence staff and said, I think you got it wrong. I think you're talking about 30 or 40 civilians from the hospital being moved. And after a bit of discussion, he told me, that's good enough. It's going to stay because you're going in for that. You're going to get it for being the Chief of Staff duties." General, where did you get this information that Leslie, Colonel Leslie, had participated in these rescue missions?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew personally that the 40 UN employees, that doesn't seem to be the case, but I remember that he went and got some people in the town, you know, early in the morning of the 4th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And who told you that?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was reported to me, I think, by either Colonel Tymchuk or Major Balfour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: By Tymchuk or Balfour?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Would it surprise you, General, to note that Colonel Leslie maintains he made one trip to find an address and picked up several UN employees and that's -- that was it?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's break time -- I'm after break time so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll have a break and we'll resume at five minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, the Chamber granted you extra time on an application. The Chamber has considered during the last break the present situation. The Chamber unanimously concluded that if we would have known the way in which you have used your time in cross-examination that we would not have granted extra time. This may appear not useful for you to know, but for future applications, it's certainly important for you to be aware of this. We're not reversing the decision. For you, Mr. Forand, even if we would not have granted extra time, we would not have finished by 12.00, so it doesn't change your situation which -- on which I expressed myself already before. Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe, you have got 59 minutes left. If you could conclude in the next 46 minutes, that would be appreciated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We encourage you to do it but the time granted is granted. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
