utterances.text: I'm going to shift gears, General, and turn to the Alun Roberts situation where you stated that General Gotovina threatened Alun Roberts for being a spy and a provocateur, I believe?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact words, it was in my sitrep.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, you do know that the animosity between Mr. Roberts and General Gotovina predated Operation Storm, do you not?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw something in what was presented to me that seemed to indicate that, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And had it been a subject of discussion about this animosity between the two of them?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean to me?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: By either one?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Either one?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General Gotovina accused Mr. Roberts of being a spy. And my question to you was: Was he?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Roberts a spy?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge. Spy for who?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was he providing information directly or indirectly to the Serbian authorities?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We will tie that up in future witnesses, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me shift gears to some of the other issues that you raised and in your testimony, you noted on page 4143, line 19, "Yes, because the looting I saw was on the 5th when I was returning from the hospital and also the looting that I saw taking place in front of the headquarters when we were surrounded. Some of the IDP had left their vehicles outside of the gate because obviously there was no place in my compound and we saw some HV troops, you know, looting the contents of those vehicles." I'd like to talk to you first about the first sentence. You were returning from the hospital on the 5th. You said "... because the looting I saw was on the 5th when I returned from the hospital." Now, let me show you first the 1D28-0150. Now, as this is coming up on the screen, General, you noted that you had picked up some ECMM individuals and brought them back to the compound; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I want you to take a look at this, this is an ECMM report for 1245 on the 5th of August. And it notes in paragraph 3 -- excuse me -- yes, paragraph 3, the 5 APCs that had gone to the hospital and their way back through town. If you can briefly go through that. And in paragraph 4, it accounts that "On the way back through the town, we were stopped by 5 HV tanks." That was your experience going back through the town, was it not, General?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 6, the ECMM individual notes that the HV soldiers appear to be professional and are treating the civilian population fairly, but I am not so sure about any soldiers they meet." Now, that is counter what you testified to concerning that drive as well -- excuse me, strike that. That's counter to what you observed during that drive, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you also noted for us during the course of your testimony that you saw 22 bodies?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And this notes three bodies that were -- excuse me -- three bodies that were not there on the outward journey, all of these were ARSK soldiers. Now, these individuals were travelling with you and they saw three bodies yet you saw 22.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: You think he says three that were not there. He doesn't say that he had not seen others before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, did you take a different route back and forth?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, same route.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I count 22. What can I say?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let us turn to -- can I offer that into evidence, Your Honour, 1D28-0150.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D334, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us turn --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D334 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us turn our attention to P345.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe. You put to the witness, you read the report in a certain way where it seems to be not unambiguous. You could read, I saw three bodies that were not there on the outward journey, or I saw three bodies that were not on the outward -- I mean you can read it two different ways. Do we agree on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We agree on that, Judge. And if we're reading it in your fashion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, not in my fashion, I read two fashions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Two fashions, yes, whatever fashion, but in any event there is no discussion of 22 bodies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. No. That's clear. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is a situation report of 5 August, 1200 hours. And if I can go to the second page of this exhibit, the next page. And by the way, this is part of the commander's assessment. And you note I just read over, HVO soldiers are now at the gates of the HQSS compound, and going to the top of this page, "The city of Knin is now completely in the hands of the HV. They entered at approximately 10.00 a.m. We were able to gather more refugees within the camp and with the compliance of the HV, we managed to move 60 sick and wounded from the Knin hospital. During the last run into Knin, the sector commander SC and party were met by Croats. Knin is full of tanks and APC. HV soldiers were not seen abusing civilians nor military but were fairly friendly." Now, that is your assessment at the time, was it not, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as written there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And there's no discussion obviously of any looting?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: But there was looting that took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me turn your attention back to the next document which is P351. This is a sitrep of 6 August, 1300. If we can move to two more pages in, three more pages in, as part of the commander's -- the general situation. This is a -- two sentences down, it notes that, "OC military police patrol entered buildings looking for evidence of looting and destruction and found little evidence of ransacking or wanton destruction. What looting there is seems limited to beer and portable radios, et cetera. Now, 20 to 25 civilians were seen carrying on life as best they could without interference from the HV." Now, once again, that was an assessment that you got from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- Captain Hill, General, and would you agree that to the extent that there was any looting, it was minor?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to him, but I know what I've seen and there was soldiers coming in and out of the stores, you know, that were on the main street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, going to D29. In the second paragraph, about midway through it says, "There is a significant HV presence ..." this is on the 7th. It notes that "There was a significant HV presence in the town, but the soldiers did not appear overly ruly; although, several were drinking beer or spirts around noon." And one last document on this score which would be P52, which is another sitrep from 2030 hours on the 6th. Now, if we can go to the last page of that document. I'm sorry, if we could go one page in. And this is a -- as I noted, General, another sitrep as of the 2030 on the 6th. In the last paragraph, again, this is a part of the sector commander's summary. In the last sentence, of the last -- of F, "More civilians including cars with Split licence plates are seen in Knin, and a sense of normalcy is returning. Tanks and APCs have disappeared to be replaced by masses of humanity [sic] --" excuse me, "masses of infantry." Excuse me. Now, in your assessment, General, by the evening of the 6th of August, had a sense of normalcy returned to Knin as you set out in this sitrep?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, based on what we were seeing on my camp because we were not allowed out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well you did -- Captain Hill was going about town, is isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he went once. I don't know if he was allowed many times after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And he provided you information as to what he saw and observed; right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the sitrep as shown, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And based on the information that you received, you concluded that a sense of normalcy had returned?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now -- and again, you note during the course of your testimony -- and the looting issue, you point to a looting of a vehicle outside of your headquarters, and again I refer you back to 4143, line 23 through 24. And if I could go to 1D28-0040. And this is a video. Yes, there is no interpretation on this Judge, I am informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, is that the incident that you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I mean I don't remember the car. There was a couple of cars, you know, that were in front so I don't remember exactly if it was that car or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, General, the automobile that you were talking about, this is the one that was in front of the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: You tell me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, you tell me. The one you're referring to, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember if that were -- there were some cars in front of the headquarter. Was it that one? I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let me --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I will tender this video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one clarifying question. You said there were some cars in front, did you see when the looting -- when you observed the looting, several cars being there or one isolated car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there was three or four cars, but I saw looting from only one car, what I considered looting. They were removing stuff from the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you remember any shooting the locks off the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it that you remember that that's not what happened or that you don't remember whether this was the way.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember if that was the way that he used to open the baggage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D335, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed. That will be admitted into evidence. That is then D335 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me read you a portion of Colonel Leslie's portion at 2191 at line 2 going through line 11. Question: "Did you in any way personally observe any looting or burning either within the city of Knin or outside the city of Knin? Answer: "Yes, sir. There were a couple of vehicles that had been abandoned by Serbs in close proximity to the headquarters. You could see some Croatian soldiers rummaging through the vehicles. I did not see any looting inside Knin with one very minor exception, and to be fair, to be fair, that one incident I saw, one could argue that that may be someone who was searching that vehicle to see if there were any explosives or such." Now, the vehicle that you saw, was that the vehicle that you -- was General Leslie observing the same thing?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he was at that time, but I would say, you know, if you think there is explosive inside, you wouldn't use a rifle to shoot at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I wouldn't say it was the wise thing to do, but were you observing the same vehicle that Colonel Leslie was observing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness has answered this question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you noted a issue of looting and there is a difference between ransacking a place and looting it, taking things away, isn't there? To your mind?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure I know the difference between ransacking and looting. To me it seems to be the same action.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let me show you a video, if I could, and this is again taken in your camp and is provided that compilation that was received by the Prosecutor and it's 1D28-0034.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Kehoe, you asked whether the witness was aware that there was a difference between ransacking and looting. Apparently you consider that there is a difference. Now the witness says "I'm not aware. For me it's all the same." For us, I'm not also not a native English speaker --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And what I'm going to do Judge is use the next video as a way of exploring that just briefly, the difference between ransacking and looting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but the witness says -- okay. Let's see what happens.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I do believe that the booths have the transcript on this.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "This woman wants to go to Knin." "Yes, she wants to leave." "Okay. When does she want to go?" "Right now." "Okay. Now is she Serb or Croat?" "She is Serb." "Does she understand that there is no water, no electricity, no telephone?" "Yes, she does." "And almost every house has been ransacked, so everything is thrown everywhere." "Yes, she knows that." "Okay. And is she living alone?" "She is living alone, but her daughter is in ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, based -- you recognise Norm Boucher in that?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. Is he a Canadian or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: He is. CIVPOL.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, the French translation of the video clip has been completed. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, when we talk about the -- what this lady was talking about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- the consequence of not waiting is that where you can read relatively easy from the text that portions of what was said after that have, as far as I am aware of, not been translated into French so would you please resume --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We can play it again, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, not -- but your questions. You can see them on the screen, "General, you recognise ..." that part is, as far as I'm aware of, is lost in the French translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I asked you, General, do you recognise Norm Boucher in that video?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. And you said is he a Canadian or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I said he is CIVPOL.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now everything is on the record. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, there -- going through Knin to your recollection, was there a degree of police and soldiers going from apartment to apartment doing security searches and in the course of that throwing items around?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that, that was in the main street and I don't think there was that many apartment within that street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was there, based on the information you received, a process of going through Knin by the HV authorities looking for weapons or booby-traps or things of that nature?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: They must have had that. They had entered Knin and I suppose as part of their order that's the first thing they would have done.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that would be based on your military experience, a normal thing that a military would do or a police department would do going through a town to secure it; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: They better do it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour can I move this video into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D336, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D336 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. And if I can turn, General, back to P401, it's a matter that we touched on yesterday, and we are shifting topics here, General. Now, in the document that you have, you note in the second paragraph -- and this is P401. It's your presentation, General, page 20, paragraph 2. Do you see that, General?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It begins by "However, we have to recognise ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, sir. The second sentence, you note that: "But, overall, I believe that the Croatians do not possess a professional army." And you were asked, yesterday on page 4350 at line 21: "General, you knew that this was an army that had just begun; isn't that right?" "Yes." "Question: And had been formed approximately a year or so ago prior to Operation Storm." "Answer: Yes, sir." General, based on your military experience, how long does it take to train a brigade-level commander?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, you have to have a brigade. It depends on what type of training, what level. If it's combat arms or if it is -- depending on the type of forces you have, it could take -- I don't know. I became a General, you know, after 25 years. So you have to build it up. Some people may be able to learn faster than others, but I would say it would take quite a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we're talking about a brigade level as part of an infantry corps, when you say "quite a while," how long are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say, because you have -- you would have to train and to do some real training and all that, from two to three years at least, to be proficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: As a brigade level commander?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And how about at the battalion level, how long would it take to be proficient?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, it could be a couple of years, depending also the rank of the individual, depending on his background and his experience. I mean, there's a lot of factor that has to be weighted in. The courses that he would have followed, I mean, you don't become a battalion commander as soon as you were enrolled in the army, you know. It takes a little while before you reach that level.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And in the Canadian Army, how long would it take to become a battalion commander once you joined the officer corps in the Canadian Armed Forces?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the other, but for me it took 15 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And at the brigade level of the Canadian army, how long would it take an officer to become a brigade level commander?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, again, it depends on the individual. I was in 1993, I was born in 1944, so 49 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Forty-nine years?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was 49 years. I mean 1967 to 1993, that's, what, 28.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Twenty-eight years?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. But, again, this is not -- it's in line, you know, with that you're competing with your confrere, and we have only three brigade in Canada. So the selection process may take a little bit longer because there's only three brigade, which normally change every two years.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But in any event, it would take a significant period of time?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: At the company level, obviously down the ladder from the brigade and the battalion level --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please pause between question and answer, and slow down for the purposes of the interpretation. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: My apologies -- our apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: At the company level --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you also please come to your point, Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. At the company level, it would, likewise, take a significant period of time?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It took me 11 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, it would take yet longer to train up this cadre of officers and commanders during a time of war, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you accelerate the process. Usually, it would be shorter because there is a lot of administration, you know, that would be thrown aside, and you would focus specifically on the combat arms training.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In any event, to do this job proficiently, it would still take a significant period of time?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Agreed, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you knew that General Gotovina was an operational commander during this -- during the time-frame that you were in Sector South; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I think you talked to us about the -- sorry. You talked to us about the operation in Bosanski Grahovo, as well as Operation Storm. Now, you noted on page 18 of your presentation at the top of the page, if you can, that Operation Storm, it says, "Let me now turn to the Croatian offensive nicknamed Operation Storm. The operation was the culmination of months of planning and preliminary moves." Now, generally, General, an operation such as that, based on your experience, would take months and months of planning for an operational commander to set up and execute, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would take a couple of months, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And given the fact that the HV was moving up the Dinara, going into Operation Storm, and then continuing activities into Bosnia after Operation Storm, General Gotovina was planning and participating in a series of offensive reactions that went on for a significant period of time, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. He did not convey to me, you know, his plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, based on what you learn, you did learn -- when you were in Sector South, you learned that there were significant offensives going up until just about the time you left in Operation Maestral in September, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was aware that it was ongoing, but I must say that I was not paying particular attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: During all of that, based on your experience, an operational commander would have by the very fact of being an operational commander involved in significant activities, planning, and executing any such offensives, wouldn't he?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: If he is the one commanding, he better be involved, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, in your 1990 -- by the way, you noted for us, during the course of your testimony on direct examination, that I think your last meeting with General Gotovina was September the 5th; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And after Operation Storm, it was the meeting on the 8th and September the 5th, and that's the only time you met with him?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And during that other period of time, did you know that he was involved in ongoing military activities against the Bosnian Serbs and the Krajina Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, in your statement -- and I'm turning now to your 1997 statement, which I believe is P331. On line 1, General, you note that: "If you're a good military organisation, there is no reason why you're not able to control your soldiers."

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which page are you looking at?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm looking at page 15 of your presentation -- excuse me, of your --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are now in P331, page 15, line 1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Got it, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You note there that: "If you're a good military organisation, there is no reason why you're not able to control your soldiers." Now, that's not what you observed on the ground; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, you didn't observe people in uniform that appeared to be under control.

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you've got to go further than the first line because my reflection of that is what I was seeing the looting and the burning. And to me, it was a lack of control because it carried on, you know, for almost a month.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's exactly what I was saying. These people in uniform, you perceive, not to be under control?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if I could turn your attention --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if I could go back to 1D28-0151, which is the red line, and if I could turn to page 16 of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let's look at the bottom of that first paragraph when you're talking about burning and looting. Do you see the sentence, "Nevertheless ..."

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I is see it, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: "Nevertheless, in these towns, specific houses and buildings were burnt, and looting was rampant. There was no apparent method to the," and you had written in your statement "to the destruction." Now, you didn't see any methodology behind that, did you, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Methodology for?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just any methodology that would give some rationale to this type of destruction, did you? Well, let me help you out a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me turn to 1D28-0007.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is a document that discusses -- this is an interview you gave to Globus Magazine, and if we go to the last page of that document. This is an article that is dated 12 March 2004. In this question under the title, There was no criminal plan: "In the indictment against the Croatian generals accused based on command responsibility for crimes committed during and after Operation Storm, it is stated they were part of a criminal enterprise; that is, that this was a planned operation intend today kill people. Do you agree with these theories?" "I would never say that there was any form of order that existed concerning a criminal plan or an idea whose purpose would be to murder civilians. Definitely not. As I said earlier, approximately 2.000 people remained in this area at the time I left Croatia. In my opinion, they were isolated cases because no form of order had been established, nor were those individuals who had committed crimes punished quickly. It is customary in the country I come from that commanders are responsible for the people subordinate to them." Now, General, consistent with this article, the crimes that you saw or observed or were being reported to, it is a fact that there was no form or order to that or planning to that, was there?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. That seems to be conflating a number of different issues. This refers to murders of civilians, one, something specific; and now it's being broadened to include everything?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's exactly right. I'm broadening the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, what you're actually doing is you're asking, if you read also the last couple of lines where the choice of this witness, that 7(3) would be more applicable than joint criminal enterprise under 7(1), is a right choice. That's actually what it comes down to. He's given joint criminal enterprise -- criminal enterprise. I don't know whether the witness has full understanding of what that means in legal terms. He explains that -- you didn't read the last two lines as far as Mr. Cermak is concerned, but he makes a reference to what appears to be superior responsibility. I don't know whether it's of great use to ask these kinds of things where the witness mainly, of course, came to testify and whatever was said in the interview. I do not oppose against asking, but I'm just drawing your attention to what the exercise comes down to at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am aware that it's a two-pronged part of this, and there is a crime against humanity charged, where there is a widespread and systematic attack on the civilian population with the approval of the state. So taking a question to the General that he didn't perceive that there was some criminal plan, but rather there was a lack of punishment and accountability on the 7(3) end, I thought and believe it was relevant for the Chamber to know as a person who was in the theatre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It requires a lot of legal skills to make such a judgement. If you consider it important, then it's your cross examination. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just note in the actual sitreps, itself, it uses term "the widespread and systematic" on the 7(1) line. I am attempting to address that through General Forand who was the sector commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's us move on, General. During the course of your time in Sector South, were you aware that General Gotovina had both professional brigades and conscripts under his command?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to remember. Somebody must have mentioned to me, that it was not all professional army, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were you aware of the specific units under his command?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. Well, I don't recall. I know that in my presentation, there's a certain numbers of unit that were put in my presentation, but I'm not aware fully, you know, about what he had under his command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You're not familiar with that command structure in the HV?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, likewise, when people were wearing uniforms, I mean, some of them were on duty and some of them were off duty, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only one I observed when I went out of the camp, you know, were those that I met in towns on the route where I was going, and they were all armed. I don't remember seeing soldiers that were not armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But you don't know, even if they had an arm, if they were on duty or off duty?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, likewise, you don't know if they had been, for instance, demobilised already?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No idea, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you wouldn't know if these individuals that you observed were just civilians wearing camouflage or fatigue clothing?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No idea either, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now you noted in your statement in 1997 if you had come across these problems -- and I'm talking about page 20 of 331. You note what you're talking about, and this is seeing these types of activities, crimes. General, I'm not quibbling with you that crimes took place. I'm not saying that at all. I'm just saying what your statement on line 3 is: "My reaction would have been simple. I'd bring into my office whoever I had under me, my Chief of Staff or the unit commander responsible in that particular area; tell him to investigate; and to report as soon as possible; and put on my desk; and come and explain to me exactly what happened." Now, on that score, General, had you observed this for soldiers under your command, you would have issued orders, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you, General, you would have yelled at people giving them an order to do their job, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have to yell to give orders, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You would firmly give your orders, telling people to do their job, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: You better believe it, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if this was going on, you would cease your -- have your subordinates cease this activity, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: ALAIN ROBERT FORAND [Resumed]
utterances.text: You better believe it, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We will consider that together with Mr. Registrar because there are all kinds of technical elements involved there. But, first of all, even if it's uploaded on to e-court, before any decision could be taken on it, the Chamber, of course, would like to have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
